Name: Aaron Weber
Bio: Standup comedian based in Nashville, TN and a regular performer at the Grand Ole Opry — the youngest comic ever to perform in the Opry circle. Originally from Montgomery, Alabama, he graduated from Notre Dame before pursuing comedy full-time. Co-hosts The Nateland Podcast with Nate Bargatze and Brian Bates, and released his debut special "Signature Dish" (executive produced by Bargatze/Nateland Entertainment).

Name: Adam Sandler
Bio: Stand-up comedian, actor, and musician from Brooklyn, New York, raised in Manchester, New Hampshire, who joined Saturday Night Live as a cast member from 1990 to 1995. Known for his everyman comic persona and novelty songs like "The Chanukah Song," he became one of Hollywood's biggest comedy stars with films including Billy Madison, Happy Gilmore, and The Wedding Singer, later earning acclaim for dramatic turns such as Uncut Gems. After decades away from the stage, he returned to stand-up with two Netflix specials, 100% Fresh (2018) and Love You (2024), and received the Kennedy Center's Mark Twain Prize for American Humor in 2023.

Name: Akaash Singh
Bio: Stand-up comedian and podcaster based in New York City, originally from Dallas, Texas. He left the pre-med track at Austin College to pursue comedy full-time, later breaking through with appearances on MTV's Wild 'n Out and Guy Code. Known for a brash, culturally pointed, crowd-work-heavy style, he built a large following co-hosting the Flagrant podcast alongside Andrew Schulz and self-releases his specials directly to YouTube, including Bring Back Apu (2022) and Gaslit (2024).

Name: Andrew Schulz
Bio: Stand-up comedian, actor, and podcaster who grew up in Manhattan's East Village and is now based in New York City. He graduated from UC Santa Barbara before building an early following through self-released, independently distributed specials on YouTube. Known for sharp, unfiltered observational and political comedy, he's since headlined sold-out arena tours and released the Netflix specials Schulz Saves America (2020) and Life (2025), along with the self-released Infamous (2022) â€” one of YouTube's most-watched comedy specials. Co-hosts the podcasts Flagrant with Akaash Singh and The Brilliant Idiots with Charlamagne Tha God.

Name: Anita Renfroe
Bio: Standup comedian and musical-comedy performer originally from Atlanta, Georgia and now based in the Texas Hill Country. Best known for her viral 2007 video "The Mom Song," a rapid-fire recitation of everyday mom phrases set to the William Tell Overture, she built her career on the Christian and family-friendly comedy circuit, touring for years with the Women of Faith conference. Known for clean, music-driven comedy about marriage and motherhood, she's released numerous comedy DVDs and books, including Total Momsense and Don't Say I Didn't Warn You: Kids, Carbs, and the Coming Hormonal Apocalypse.

Name: Anjelah Johnson-Reyes
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actress born and raised in San Jose, California. Before comedy, she was an NFL cheerleader for the Oakland Raiderettes, earning Rookie of the Year honors and performing at Super Bowl XXXVII, before relocating to Los Angeles in 2005 to pursue comedy full-time. She rose to fame on MADtv, best known for character-based sketches like "Bon Qui Qui" and her nail salon bits, and has since released seven stand-up specials, including Say I Won't (2023) and Technically Not Stalking (2024), plus the podcast Funjelah.

Name: Bert Kreischer
Bio: Stand-up comedian and podcaster born in St. Petersburg, Florida and raised in Tampa, who spent six years at Florida State University and became the subject of a notorious 1997 Rolling Stone profile chronicling a college trip to Russia â€” the origin of his signature story and nickname, "The Machine," later adapted into a 2023 action-comedy film of the same name. Known for shirtless, high-energy storytelling built around outrageous personal anecdotes, he's released stand-up specials for Comedy Central and Netflix, including Secret Time (2018), Hey Big Boy (2020), and Razzle Dazzle (2023). Co-hosts the podcast 2 Bears, 1 Cave with Tom Segura and produces his own show, Bertcast.

Name: Bill Cosby
Bio: Stand-up comedian and storyteller from Philadelphia, PA, who served in the U.S. Navy before earning degrees from Temple University and UMass Amherst. He began performing in Philadelphia and New York clubs in the early 1960s, building his reputation on observational, conversational storytelling about childhood and family life rather than topical material. He holds the record for the most Grammy Awards for Best Comedy Album and is closely associated with the animated series Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids, which he created, and the sitcom The Cosby Show. His concert film Bill Cosby: Himself (1983) is widely regarded as one of the most influential stand-up specials ever made.

Name: Bill Engvall
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor originally from Galveston, Texas, now based in Park City, Utah. Best known for his signature "Here's Your Sign" bit, he co-founded the Blue Collar Comedy Tour in 2000 alongside Jeff Foxworthy, Larry the Cable Guy, and Ron White. Created and starred in The Bill Engvall Show (2007â€“2009) and later joined the cast of Last Man Standing. Built a decades-long stand-up catalog anchored by his platinum-certified debut album Here's Your Sign (1996), and closed out his touring career with the farewell special Here's Your Sign, It's Finally Time â€” My Last Show (2023).

Name: Jeff Foxworthy
Bio: Stand-up comedian born and raised near Atlanta, Georgia, who spent five years in mainframe computer maintenance at IBM before winning Atlanta's Great Southeastern Laugh-Off in 1984 and turning to comedy full-time. Best known for his "You Might Be a Redneck Ifâ€¦" one-liners and as a founding member of the Blue Collar Comedy Tour alongside Larry the Cable Guy, Bill Engvall, and Ron White, he's billed as the largest-selling comedy-recording artist in history. Beyond stand-up, he's hosted the game show Are You Smarter Than a 5th Grader? and written the autobiography No Shirt, No Shoesâ€¦ No Problem!, and continues to tour behind his latest special, The Joke's On Me (2026).

Name: Bob Saget
Bio: Stand-up comedian, actor, and director born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, best known to mainstream audiences as wholesome single dad Danny Tanner on Full House and as the original host of America's Funniest Home Videos. Behind that squeaky-clean TV image, he built a parallel career as an unapologetically raunchy stand-up comic, a contrast he leaned into throughout his live shows and specials including That's What I'm Talkin' About (2013, Grammy-nominated) and Zero to Sixty (2017). He also hosted the podcast Bob Saget's Here For You. He died on January 9, 2022, at age 65, while on a stand-up tour.

Name: Brad Stine
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor based near Nashville, TN, raised in Bremen, Indiana. Nicknamed "God's Comic" after an 8-page New Yorker profile, he's built a three-decade career on a rapid-fire, politically conservative and Christian-inflected comedic style taking aim at political correctness and cancel culture. He's released numerous stand-up specials and DVDs, including Tolerate This!, Wussification, and his most recent, Laugh While It's Legal (2025), and hosts the podcast Brad Stine Has Issues.

Name: Brad Williams
Bio: Stand-up comedian from Orange County, California, based in the Los Angeles area, born with achondroplasia (a form of dwarfism), which is central to his self-deprecating comedic style. He got his start at 19 when Carlos Mencia pulled him onstage during a live show, and went on to become the first stand-up comedian to headline a Cirque du Soleil production, "Mad Apple," in Las Vegas. He's released multiple one-hour specials â€” most recently Starfish (2023) and Live On Short Street (2026) â€” appeared in Netflix's stand-up showcase The Degenerates (2018), and co-hosts the podcast Heightened Babble with JB Ball.

Name: Bron Lewis
Bio: Melbourne, Australia-based stand-up comedian and writer, and a former high school teacher before pursuing comedy full-time. Co-winner of the National Raw Comedy competition in 2022, she was nominated for the Melbourne International Comedy Festival's Best Newcomer award in 2023 following her sold-out debut show, Probably. She's a writer for The Project and a regular panellist on Have You Been Paying Attention?, and her stand-up frequently draws on her life as a mother of three navigating parenting and everyday absurdities, most recently in her specials Obviously (2024) and Who's Talking?! (2025).

Name: Chad Daniels
Bio: Stand-up comedian and Minnesota native who still bases himself in his hometown of Fergus Falls. He got his start in 1998 at open-mic nights at ACME Comedy Company in Minneapolis, developing a deadpan, self-deprecating style built on dry Midwestern humor about marriage, fatherhood, and small-town life. Three of his comedy albums have cracked the Billboard comedy top 10, and he's one of only 13 comics ever to appear on The Tonight Show with Conan O'Brien. He co-hosts the podcasts Pretend Problems and Middle of Somewhere, and released his Netflix debut special, Empty Nester, in 2024.

Name: Chonda Pierce
Bio: Stand-up comedian based near Nashville, Tennessee, known as comedy's "Queen of Clean" for her family-friendly, faith-rooted humor. Born in Covington, Kentucky and raised in South Carolina as a preacher's daughter, she got her start at Nashville's Opryland Theme Park before building a solo career that made her the RIAA's top-selling female comedian of all time, with 14 gold/platinum-certified DVDs. She's been openly candid about her struggles with depression, chronicling the deaths of her mother and husband in the 2015 documentary Chonda Pierce: Laughing in the Dark, and has founded Branches Recovery Center to provide counseling for depression, anxiety, and addiction.

Name: Chris D'Elia
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor known for his animated, character-driven delivery, with a career breakout as Danny Burton on NBC's Undateable and a memorable arc on Comedy Central's Workaholics. Born in Montclair, New Jersey and raised largely in Los Angeles, he briefly attended NYU before leaving to pursue comedy, performing his first stand-up set in 2006. He's released five one-hour specials â€” including Incorrigible (2015), Man on Fire (2017), and Grow or Die (2023) â€” and hosts the long-running podcast Congratulations with Chris D'Elia.

Name: Christina P
Bio: Stand-up comedian and podcaster born in Windsor, Ontario, Canada, and raised largely in Southern California. Known for a blunt, high-energy delivery tearing into marriage, motherhood, and aging, she came up through LA comedy clubs before headlining nationally. She co-hosts the long-running Your Mom's House podcast with her husband, comedian Tom Segura, and has released two Netflix hour specials, Mother Inferior (2017) and Mom Genes (2022).

Name: Christopher Titus
Bio: Stand-up comedian known for what he calls "hard funny" â€” unflinchingly dark, autobiographical material drawn from a turbulent upbringing, including an alcoholic father and a mother who died by suicide. Born in Castro Valley, California, his one-man show Norman Rockwell is Bleeding became the basis for the FOX sitcom Titus (2000â€“2002), which he starred in, co-created, and executive produced. One of stand-up's most prolific special-makers, he's self-released a new hour-plus special almost every year since 2004, including Neverlution, Angry Pursuit of Happiness, and 2024's Carrying Monsters, his tenth.

Name: Daniel Sloss
Bio: Scottish stand-up comedian from Fife, who began performing as a teenager and became one of the youngest comedians to headline a solo season at London's Soho Theatre and in the West End. Known for dark, brutally honest, deeply personal storytelling, he built an international following through the Netflix specials DARK and Jigsaw (both 2018) and the HBO special X (2019). He's since self-released further acclaimed specials directly through his own website, including SOCIO (2022), HUBRIS (2024), and CAN'T (2025).

Name: Daren Streblow
Bio: Stand-up comedian and radio host based in Minnesota, known for clean, family-friendly observational comedy in the style of Brian Regan and Jerry Seinfeld. Originally from Ely, Minnesota, he started in radio as a teenager before turning to stand-up in 1995 at Acme Comedy Company in Minneapolis, going full-time by 1998. He hosts the nationally syndicated Daren Streblow Comedy Show, airing in over 70 radio markets, and has released two hour-long specials through Dry Bar Comedy: Organic and Inorganic Life (2019) and Wives Talk Too Much (2020).

Name: Drew Lynch
Bio: Stand-up comedian best known for finishing runner-up on America's Got Talent Season 10 (2015), where Howie Mandel awarded him the Golden Buzzer. Originally from Indianapolis, Indiana, he developed a neurogenic stutter at age 20 after being struck in the throat by a softball, and turned to stand-up as part of his recovery, building a self-deprecating act around the stutter itself. He also hosts the long-running YouTube series Dog Vlog (starring his service dog, Stella) and the podcast Did I Stutter?!, and has released several hour-long specials distributed free on his own YouTube channel, including Concussed (2021) and The Stuttering Comedian (2025).

Name: Dustin Nickerson
Bio: Stand-up comedian based in San Diego, California, known for clean, family-friendly comedy centered on marriage, parenting, and domestic life. Originally from the Seattle, Washington area, he graduated from the University of Washington before building a following through clubs, colleges, and the Christian-comedy circuit. His debut special, Overwhelmed (2020), became one of Amazon Prime Video's highest-rated comedy specials, and he's since released additional specials including It Runs in the Family (2023). He co-hosts the podcast Don't Make Me Come Back There with his wife, Melissa, which joined Nate Bargatze's Nateland Podcast Network in 2024.

Name: Gabriel Iglesias
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor who grew up in Long Beach, California, known worldwide by the nickname "Fluffy" â€” coined from an early bit about his weight ("I'm not fat, I'm fluffy") that became his signature brand. His act blends storytelling, sound effects, and character voices, and he's become one of the highest-grossing touring comedians in the world, making history in 2022 as the first comic to headline and sell out a Major League Baseball stadium (Dodger Stadium). He's released numerous Netflix specials, including I'm Sorry for What I Said When I Was Hungry (2016), Stadium Fluffy (2022), and Legend of Fluffy (2025), and starred in the Netflix sitcom Mr. Iglesias (2019â€“2020).

Name: Gina Brillon
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actress raised in the Bronx, New York, of Puerto Rican descent, who began performing at 17 after her mother entered her and her twin sister in a local comedy contest. She became the first Latina to win NBC's Stand Up for Diversity showcase in 2012, and in 2021 made history as the first Latina comedian to reach the finals of America's Got Talent (Season 16). Known for a high-energy, story-driven style rooted in her New York upbringing, she's released four one-hour specials, including The Floor Is Lava (2020, Gracie Award winner) and Mind Your Business (2025).

Name: Greg Davies
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor from Wem, Shropshire, England, who worked as a secondary school drama teacher for roughly 13 years before turning to comedy full-time. Known for his towering 6'8" frame, often used as a comedic device, and a loud, exasperated stage persona, he's widely recognized for playing Mr. Gilbert in The Inbetweeners and for hosting the BAFTA-winning panel show Taskmaster since 2015. His stand-up work includes the Edinburgh Comedy Award-nominated debut Firing Cheeseballs at a Dog, The Back of My Mum's Head, and the Netflix special You Magnificent Beast.

Name: Henry Cho
Bio: Korean-American stand-up comedian born and raised in Knoxville, Tennessee, best known for pairing his Southern drawl with his Korean heritage. He attended the University of Tennessee before breaking into comedy in 1986, going on to national television appearances including The Tonight Show. A committed clean comic who works without profanity, he's performed at the Grand Ole Opry more than 100 times and in 2023 became the first Asian-American inducted as an Opry member. His filmed special, Henry Cho: What's That Clickin' Noise? (2006), aired on Comedy Central and later streamed on Netflix.

Name: Iliza Shlesinger
Bio: Stand-up comedian raised in Dallas, Texas, who trained with ComedySportz before attending Emerson College in Boston. In 2008 she became the first woman â€” and the youngest ever â€” to win NBC's Last Comic Standing, building a career on sharp observational humor about dating, womanhood, and generational identity. She's released seven stand-up specials, six for Netflix (including War Paint, Elder Millennial, and Hot Forever) plus 2025's A Different Animal for Amazon Prime, and hosts the podcast Ask Iliza Anything.

Name: JB Ball
Bio: Stand-up comedian and TV/sketch writer from Tampa, Florida, who has also worked as a segment producer on Kevin Hart's Ridiculousness and toured as an opener for Hart. Named 2014's "Florida's Funniest Comedian" and a 2016 Just For Laughs Montreal "New Faces" showcase pick, his comedy is billed as deceptively edgy and intelligent, mining humor from controversial and topical subjects. He co-hosts the podcast Heightened Babble with Brad Williams, and has released two hour-long specials, It's My Privilege (2023) and Jesus in the Crackhouse (2025).

Name: Jack Whitehall
Bio: British comedian, actor, and writer born in London, part of a comedy dynasty â€” his father, Michael Whitehall, is a recurring on-screen foil throughout his career. Known for his posh, self-deprecating persona, he co-wrote and starred as Alfie Wickers in the BBC sitcom Bad Education, and found crossover success with the Netflix travel series Jack Whitehall: Travels with My Father. He's released multiple Netflix stand-up specials, including At Large (2017), I'm Only Joking (2020, filmed at Wembley Stadium), and Settle Down (2024, filmed at London's O2 Arena).

Name: James Acaster
Bio: Stand-up comedian from Kettering, Northamptonshire, England, who played drums in local bands before turning to comedy full-time in 2008. Known for a surreal, absurdist, and meticulously structured storytelling style, he holds the record for the most consecutive Best Comedy Show nominations at the Edinburgh Fringe (five, 2012â€“2016) and became a familiar panel-show face on Mock the Week and Would I Lie to You?. His Edinburgh material was reworked into Netflix's four-part special series Repertoire (2018), and he co-hosts the hit podcast Off Menu with Ed Gamble.

Name: Jeff Allen
Bio: Clean, family-oriented stand-up comedian born in Sauk Village, Illinois, who began performing in Chicago comedy clubs in 1978. Sober since 1987 and a born-again Christian since 1997, he built his act around his "Happy Wife, Happy Life" philosophy, mining his own marriage, family, and faith struggles for material. He's released multiple Dry Bar Comedy specials with a claimed 400+ million combined video views, and authored the memoir Are We There Yet?: My Journey from a Messed-Up to Meaningful Life.

Name: Jeff Dye
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor from the Seattle, Washington area, known for a charming, goofy crowd-work style. He broke through nationally in 2008 as a finalist on NBC's Last Comic Standing season 6, and later hosted MTV's Money From Strangers and Fox's Who the Bleep Is That? (2023). His stand-up work includes the special How I See It (2022) and his debut full-hour video special The Last Cowboy in LA (2024), produced with 800 Pound Gorilla Records.

Name: Jen Brister
Bio: British stand-up comedian based in Brighton, a fixture on the UK circuit since the mid-1990s and a regular panelist on Mock the Week and Live at the Apollo. Openly gay, she is mother to twin sons with her partner Chloe Martin, conceived via IVF â€” a subject she mines heavily in her stand-up alongside queer family life, marriage, and aging. Her stand-up hours include Meaningless (2018), Under Privilege (2019), and The Optimist (released as a filmed special in 2023), and she co-hosts the podcasts Memory Lane and Women Talking Bollocks.

Name: Jim Gaffigan
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor known for clean, self-deprecating, food-obsessed observational comedy, including his signature bit voicing an imagined audience member reacting to his own jokes. Raised in Chesterton, Indiana, he moved to New York City in 1990 to pursue comedy after working in advertising by day and taking acting classes at night. He's released more than a dozen hour-long specials over two decades, co-created and starred in the semi-autobiographical The Jim Gaffigan Show (TV Land, 2015â€“2016), and is a bestselling author of humor books including Dad Is Fat (2013), drawing heavily on his life as a father of five.

Name: Jimmy Carr
Bio: Stand-up comedian known for rapid-fire, dark, taboo-skirting one-liners and his distinctive laugh. Born in Isleworth, London and raised in Buckinghamshire, he graduated from Cambridge and worked as a marketing executive before leaving corporate life around 2000 to pursue comedy full-time. Long-running host of the panel show 8 Out of 10 Cats (2005â€“2021) and its Countdown spin-off, he's toured continuously for two decades and released numerous filmed specials, including four for Netflix: Funny Business, The Best Of, Ultimate, Gold, Greatest Hits, His Dark Material, and Natural Born Killer.

Name: Jo Koy
Bio: Filipino-American stand-up comedian and actor raised by his single mother, Josie, in Tacoma, Washington, after spending part of his childhood in the Philippines. Much of his act centers on stories about his mom and his son, and he's built a reputation as one of the biggest live draws in comedy â€” in 2024 he set the record for most sold-out headlining shows by a comedian at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles. His 2020 Netflix special In His Elements was filmed on location in Manila, spotlighting Filipino culture and performers, and he starred in the 2022 film Easter Sunday.

Name: John Branyan
Bio: Veteran clean and Christian-circuit stand-up comedian, performing since the early 1990s, best known for a mock-Shakespearean rendition of The Three Little Pigs â€” a viral routine adapted into the book A Triune Tale of Diminutive Swine â€” along with a companion Goldilocks bit in the same style. He's released multiple stand-up specials through Dry Bar Comedy drawing heavily on family life and parenting material, and he and his wife, Lori, have four children and eleven grandchildren.

Name: John Crist
Bio: Stand-up comedian from Lilburn, Georgia, best known for viral Christian-culture and observational sketch videos, including "Every Parent at Disney" and "Christian Music: How It's Made," that have amassed over a billion combined views. A graduate of Samford University, he broke out through the Christian comedy circuit before relocating to Nashville, Tennessee, where he now bases his touring career. He hosts the podcast Net Positive with John Crist and has released four full-length stand-up specials, most recently Emotional Support (2025), and authored the 2022 book Delete That (and Other Failed Attempts to Look Good Online).

Name: John Mulaney
Bio: Stand-up comedian, writer, and actor originally from Chicago, Illinois, who graduated from Georgetown University before moving to New York to pursue comedy full-time. Rose to prominence as a Saturday Night Live writer from 2008 to 2013, co-creating the recurring character Stefon with Bill Hader, and later brought his meticulously written, storytelling-driven stand-up to Broadway with Oh, Hello alongside longtime friend and fellow Georgetown alum Nick Kroll. Built his reputation through a string of acclaimed Netflix specials, winning multiple Emmy Awards for his comedy writing, and currently creates, hosts, and executive produces the Netflix live variety talk show Everybody's Live with John Mulaney.

Name: Jonnie W
Bio: Clean comedian based in Nashville, Tennessee, known for blending storytelling, off-beat stand-up, and live music into his act. He got his start as a Young Adults Pastor at church before transitioning to comedy full-time, and has since toured 48 states â€” comedy clubs, churches, corporate events, and leadership conferences â€” and opened for Nate Bargatze on his Be Funny and Big Dumb Eyes arena tours. He's performed on the Grand Ole Opry's Circle Network and co-hosts the podcast Talk About That with John Driver.

Name: Jose Sarduy
Bio: Stand-up comedian and U.S. Air Force veteran (Lieutenant Colonel) best known for blending military stories with comedy about his Cuban-American upbringing. Born in Las Tunas, Cuba, he was brought to Miami as a young child via the Mariel boatlift, and later became a combat pilot at the U.S. Air Force Academy, serving in Operations Enduring Freedom and Iraqi Freedom. He began performing stand-up while still on active duty, going on to win the Rocky Mountain Laugh Off (2011), and has released two Dry Bar Comedy specials, Cuban Pilot and The Whitest Cuban You've Ever Seen.

Name: Josh Blue
Bio: Stand-up comedian born in Cameroon and raised in Saint Paul, Minnesota, known for his self-deprecating comedy about living with cerebral palsy. Won Season 4 of NBC's Last Comic Standing in 2006, which launched his career as a full-time touring headliner, and before comedy competed on the U.S. Paralympic soccer team at the 2004 Athens Games. He's released a string of stand-up specials â€” including Sticky Change (2012), Delete (2016), and Freak Accident (2024) â€” and still performs 200+ shows a year.

Name: Josh Wolf
Bio: Stand-up comedian based in the Las Vegas area, where he holds a long-running residency at Jimmy Kimmel's Comedy Club. Originally from Boston, Massachusetts, he attended Trinity University before moving to Los Angeles to pursue comedy, becoming a longtime round-table regular on E!'s Chelsea Lately and After Lately. Known for road-tested, observational stand-up, he's released a string of one-hour specials including Father of the Year (2019) and Here for the Fun (2023), and co-hosts the podcast Hey Maaaan with his son, Jacob Wolf.

Name: K-Von
Bio: Half-Persian stand-up comedian and actor born in Reno, Nevada, to an Iranian immigrant father and an American mother, raised largely in Las Vegas. He graduated from the University of Nevada, Reno before pursuing comedy full-time, later appearing on MTV's Disaster Date and NBC's Last Comic Standing. Branding himself "the most famous half-Persian comedian," he's built a large following through prolific self-produced and self-released specials mining the culture clash between his Persian and Middle-American upbringing, and wrote and directed the comedic documentary Nowruz: Lost & Found.

Name: Kathleen Madigan
Bio: Stand-up comedian from the St. Louis, Missouri area, one of seven children in a large Irish Catholic family. Known for her dry, sarcastic, road-warrior style built on decades of relentless touring, she has the unique distinction of being both a contestant and a judge on NBC's Last Comic Standing, and has twice toured with the USO to entertain troops in Iraq and Afghanistan. She's released numerous specials over a 25+ year career â€” including Bothering Jesus (Netflix), Hunting Bigfoot, and The Family Thread (both Prime Video) â€” and hosts the podcast Madigan's Pubcast.

Name: Kelsey Cook
Bio: Stand-up comedian originally from Spokane, Washington, who began performing while a student at Washington State University before relocating to Los Angeles to pursue comedy full-time. Known for a confessional, self-deprecating style centered on dating, relationships, and family, she often traces her material back to being raised by an International Yo-Yo Champion father and a Professional Foosball World Champion mother. She's appeared multiple times on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, co-hosts the podcast Pretend Problems with fellow comedian Chad Daniels, and has released two hour-long specials, The Hustler (2023) and Mark Your Territory (2025).

Name: Kenn Kington
Bio: Clean and Christian-comedy circuit stand-up comedian based in Kennesaw, Georgia, who has performed for over 30 years, including sets in more than 1,000 churches nationwide. Known for family- and faith-friendly storytelling humor about marriage, parenting, and everyday chaos, he's a frequently-played act on SiriusXM radio and has appeared on Comedy Central. His credits include two Netflix specials, the Dry Bar Comedy special Enjoying Chaos (2021), and the Amazon Prime special Wow Moments, which won a Golden Crown award.

Name: Kevin Hart
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor born and raised in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, who built his reputation on high-energy, physically animated storytelling rooted in family and everyday-life material. He's widely regarded as one of the highest-grossing touring comedians in the world, having released a string of specials including Laugh at My Pain, Let Me Explain, and Irresponsible. Beyond stand-up, he starred in the Ride Along and Central Intelligence film franchises and hosts the sports interview series Cold as Balls, and founded the production company Hartbeat.

Name: Kevin James
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor known as an "everyman" physical and observational comic. Born in Mineola, Long Island, New York, he broke out playing Doug Heffernan on the CBS sitcom The King of Queens (1998â€“2007) and became a box-office star with the Paul Blart: Mall Cop franchise. A frequent collaborator with Adam Sandler's Happy Madison Productions, he's appeared in films including Grown Ups and the Hotel Transylvania series. His stand-up specials include Sweat the Small Stuff (2001), the Netflix special Never Don't Give Up (2018), and the Prime Video special Irregardless (2024).

Name: Leanne Morgan
Bio: Stand-up comedian from East Tennessee known for her Southern, self-deprecating take on marriage, motherhood, and midlife. Before comedy, she spent years as a door-to-door jewelry saleswoman, where her jokes about family life with customers eventually led to paid comedy bookings â€” stardom didn't arrive until her late 50s. Her 2023 Netflix debut special, I'm Every Woman, became a breakout hit, followed by a second special, Unspeakable Things (2025), and she went on to co-create, executive produce, and star in Leanne, a Netflix sitcom based on her life.

Name: Matt Rife
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor from Ohio who started performing at 14 and skipped college to pursue comedy full-time. He built an early national profile as a cast member on MTV's Wild 'n Out before a wave of viral TikTok clips of his crowd work turned him into one of the fastest-rising names in comedy, driving a record-breaking arena tour and sold-out shows at venues like Madison Square Garden. His 2023 Netflix debut special, Natural Selection, drew significant backlash for a joke referencing domestic violence, followed by a widely criticized mock apology; he's continued releasing crowd-work-focused specials on Netflix, including Lucid â€“ A Crowd Work Special (2024) and Unwrapped (2025).

Name: Michael Ian Black
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor raised in Hillsborough, New Jersey, who attended NYU's Tisch School of the Arts before leaving to join a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles promotional tour. Got his start as a founding member of MTV's sketch troupe The State, later co-created and starred in Comedy Central's Stella, and became widely recognized for his dry, deadpan commentary on VH1's I Love the 80s. A prolific author of humor books and memoirs, he's also known for playing McKinley in Wet Hot American Summer and its Netflix follow-ups, and has released stand-up specials including Very Famous (2011) and Noted Expert (2016).

Name: Michael Jr
Bio: Clean and faith-based stand-up comedian and "comedic thought leader" known for using comedy as a bridge to purpose and deeper conversation, with material designed to work equally in comedy clubs and churches. He rose to wider prominence via his TEDx talk "More Than Funny," which uses the structure of a comedic setup and punchline as a metaphor for life purpose and has drawn millions of views on YouTube. He's appeared on The Tonight Show and Jimmy Kimmel Live!, starred in the 2020 faith-based film Selfie Dad, and authored the book Funny How Life Works.

Name: Michael McIntyre
Bio: Stand-up comedian and television presenter from London, England, known for observational comedy about everyday domestic minutiae and relatable family life. One of the UK's best-selling live comedians, he's sold over 4 million tour tickets and holds the record for most sold-out shows at London's O2 Arena. He hosts the BBC One series Michael McIntyre's Big Show and The Wheel, and broke through nationally after a standout performance at the 2006 Royal Variety Performance. His work includes multiple bestselling DVD releases, the 2020 Netflix special Showman, and two memoirs, Life & Laughing and A Funny Life.

Name: Mike Birbiglia
Bio: Stand-up comedian and storyteller from Shrewsbury, Massachusetts, who graduated from Georgetown University in 2000 before moving to New York to pursue comedy full-time. Known for long-form storytelling comedy that blends stand-up with theater, much of his material centers on his REM sleep behavior disorder â€” including the real-life incident in which he sleepwalked and ran through a second-story hotel window. A regular contributor to NPR's This American Life, he's turned six one-man shows into Netflix specials, including Sleepwalk with Me, The New One, and The Old Man & The Pool, several of which also ran on and off Broadway.

Name: Nate Bargatze
Bio: Stand-up comedian raised in the Old Hickory neighborhood of Nashville, Tennessee, known for a clean, deadpan, everyman storytelling style built around rambling, hyper-specific tangents about family and daily life. He cut his teeth in NYC clubs in the mid-2000s before breaking through nationally via his 2017 episode of Netflix's The Standups, followed by the specials The Tennessee Kid (2019) and the Grammy-nominated The Greatest Average American (2021). He's become one of the highest-grossing arena and stadium comedians in the world, has twice hosted Saturday Night Live, and in 2023 founded the family-friendly production company Nateland Entertainment.

Name: Norm Macdonald
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor born in Quebec City, Canada, best known for his deadpan, absurdist delivery and his run anchoring Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update from 1994 to 1998 â€” a tenure that ended abruptly amid his relentless O.J. Simpson jokes, which he long maintained got him fired. A beloved fixture of late-night and talk-show couches, he was known for meandering, shaggy-dog style storytelling with hosts like David Letterman and Conan O'Brien. His film work includes a starring role in the cult comedy Dirty Work (1998), and he authored the surreal, fact-bending memoir Based on a True Story: Not a Memoir (2016). He died in September 2021 after privately battling leukemia for nearly a decade, with a final special, Nothing Special, released posthumously on Netflix in 2022.

Name: Pete Holmes
Bio: Stand-up comedian and podcaster known for a goofy, high-energy, voice-heavy delivery, best known as host of the long-running interview podcast You Made It Weird. Born in Boston and raised in Lexington, Massachusetts in an evangelical Christian household, he originally planned to become a youth pastor before pursuing comedy; a painful divorce from his college girlfriend later became the basis for his semi-autobiographical HBO series Crashing (2017â€“2019), created with Judd Apatow. He's released a series of stand-up specials for Comedy Central and HBO, and has done extensive voice work on animated series including American Dad! and The Secret Life of Pets 2.

Name: Preacher Lawson
Bio: Stand-up comedian and YouTuber born in Portland, Oregon and raised largely in Orlando, Florida after his family moved frequently throughout his childhood, now based in Los Angeles. Started writing jokes at 16, going on to win the 2016 Seattle International Comedy Competition before breaking through nationally as a Top 10 finalist on America's Got Talent Season 12 (2017) and returning for AGT: The Champions. Known for a high-energy, physical, impression-heavy stand-up style, he's built a large YouTube following beyond comedy clubs with comedic travel and cooking vlogs. He's released two specials, Get to Know Me (2019, BET+) and the self-released My Name Is Preacher (2024).

Name: Ricky Gervais
Bio: Stand-up comedian, actor, writer, and producer from Reading, Berkshire, England, now based in Hampstead, London. He studied philosophy at University College London and worked in music management and radio before co-creating the mockumentary sitcom The Office (2001) with Stephen Merchant, launching a career built on cringe comedy, philosophical provocation, and a willingness to court controversy â€” most visibly across five stints hosting the Golden Globes. Beyond stand-up, he's created and starred in Extras, Derek, and the Netflix dramedy After Life, and co-hosts the podcast The Ricky Gervais Show. His stand-up catalog spans two decades of filmed specials, including the UK tours Animals, Politics, and Fame, and the Netflix specials Humanity (2018), SuperNature (2022), and Armageddon (2023), for which he won a Golden Globe for Best Stand-Up.

Name: Rob Schneider
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor born in San Francisco and raised in Pacifica, California, who began performing in Bay Area clubs while still in high school. He joined Saturday Night Live as a writer and cast member from 1988 to 1994, creating characters like "The Richmeister," before becoming a fixture of Adam Sandler's films â€” often reprising his "You can do it!" catchphrase â€” and headlining the Deuce Bigalow franchise. Known for broad, character-driven physical comedy, he's released the Netflix specials Soy Sauce and the Holocaust (2013) and Asian Momma, Mexican Kids (2020), and the Fox Nation special Woke Up in America (2023).

Name: Ron White
Bio: Stand-up comedian nicknamed "Tater Salad," born in Fritch, Texas, who served in the U.S. Navy before turning to comedy. He became a charter member of the Blue Collar Comedy Tour in the early 2000s alongside Jeff Foxworthy, Bill Engvall, and Larry the Cable Guy, building a national following on wry, cigar-and-scotch-fueled storytelling about drinking, marriage, and Southern life. His stand-up catalog includes the DVDs They Call Me "Tater Salad" (2004), You Can't Fix Stupid (2006), Behavioral Problems (2009), and A Little Unprofessional (2012), along with the Netflix special If You Quit Listening, I'll Shut Up (2018). He's also acted in Reno 911!, Sex and the City 2, and the Netflix series Tires (2025).

Name: Russell Howard
Bio: British stand-up comedian and TV host from Bath, Somerset, raised in nearby Radstock and now based in London. He studied economics at the University of the West of England before breaking through via BBC Radio 1's The Milk Run in 2004 and winning Best CompÃ¨re at the Chortle Awards in 2006. Known for a high-energy, physically animated take on topical and political material, he became a longtime panelist on Mock the Week and has hosted his own shows, Russell Howard's Good News and The Russell Howard Hour, plus the podcast Five Brilliant Things. His filmed specials include Recalibrate (2017, Netflix), Lubricant (2021, Netflix), and Live at the London Palladium (2025).

Name: Russell Peters
Bio: Stand-up comedian born in Toronto, Ontario to Anglo-Indian immigrant parents, now based in Los Angeles. He worked as a club DJ before turning to stand-up, and became an international star almost by accident when unauthorized footage of his 2004 special Comedy Now! went viral on YouTube. Known for observational comedy built on racial, ethnic, and cultural stereotypes and sharp accent work, he became the first comedian to release a Netflix stand-up special with Notorious (2013), following it with Almost Famous (2016, Netflix), Deported (2020, Prime Video), and the Patreon-streamed Act Your Age: Live in Abu Dhabi (2024). He's also produced the Peabody Awardâ€“winning documentary series Hip-Hop Evolution and voiced characters on Bob's Burgers and BoJack Horseman.

Name: Sarah Millican
Bio: British stand-up comedian from South Shields, England, who worked as a civil servant at a jobcentre until age 29. After her divorce, she took up comedy writing workshops at Newcastle's Live Theatre, and her 2008 Edinburgh Fringe debut, Sarah Millican's Not Nice, won the if.comedy Award for Best Newcomer. Known for warm, frank, Geordie-voiced observational comedy about relationships, sex, and body image, she's hosted The Sarah Millican Television Programme and the BBC Radio 4 series Sarah Millican's Support Group. Her DVD releases include the record-breaking Chatterbox (2011) and Home Bird (2014), and she's continued self-releasing specials directly through her own website, most recently Bobby Dazzler (2023) and her Netflix debut, Late Bloomer (2026).

Name: Shane Gillis
Bio: Stand-up comedian, actor, and podcaster from Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania, now based in Austin, Texas. He worked as a car salesman and an English teacher in Spain before turning to comedy, building a following through Philadelphia clubs and his popular Matt and Shane's Secret Podcast. Hired for Saturday Night Live in 2019, he was let go days later after resurfaced clips from an earlier podcast â€” a controversy he later addressed by returning to host SNL in 2024. Known for dark, self-deprecating, politically incorrect humor, he co-created and stars in the Netflix series Tires and has released the specials Live in Austin (2021, self-released to YouTube) and Beautiful Dogs (2023, Netflix).

Name: Tammy Pescatelli
Bio: Stand-up comedian raised in the Cleveland, Ohio suburbs in a large Italian-American family, now based in Meadville, Pennsylvania. She worked in morning radio and local TV before breaking through as a top-six finalist on NBC's Last Comic Standing (2004) and winning Comedy Central's Stand-Up Showdown (2010). Known for bold, sarcastic, family-centered comedy about marriage and in-laws, she created and starred in the WE tv reality series A Stand-Up Mother and appeared in the Netflix film Nonnas (2025) alongside Vince Vaughn. She's released the specials Finding the Funny (2013, Netflix) and The Way After School Special (2020).

Name: Taylor Tomlinson
Bio: Stand-up comedian raised in Temecula, California, now based in Los Angeles, who took her first stand-up class at 16 and committed to comedy full-time at 19. She broke through as a Top 10 finalist on Last Comic Standing (2015) before building a following on frank, self-deprecating material about dating, faith, and her bipolar II diagnosis. In 2024 she became the only woman hosting a late-night network comedy show, taking over CBS's After Midnight. She's released four Netflix specials â€” Quarter-Life Crisis (2020), Look At You (2022), Have It All (2024), and Prodigal Daughter (2026) â€” and co-hosts the podcasts Self-Helpless and Sad in the City.

Name: Theo Von
Bio: Stand-up comedian and podcaster from Covington, Louisiana, now based in Nashville, Tennessee. Before comedy he appeared on MTV's Road Rules and competed on four seasons of The Challenge, later winning Comedy Central's Reality Bites Back (2008) over comedians including Amy Schumer and Bert Kreischer. Known for surreal, stream-of-consciousness Southern storytelling, he hosts the podcast This Past Weekend, one of the most-streamed shows in the country. He's released the Netflix specials No Offense (2016) and Regular People (2021).

Name: Tim Hawkins
Bio: Clean, family-friendly stand-up comedian from St. Charles, Missouri, still based in the St. Louis area with his wife and four children. A former Olive Garden waiter, he was encouraged by coworkers to try an open mic before going full-time into comedy in the early 2000s, building a following on the Christian and family-comedy circuit and through viral musical-parody videos like "Pretty Pink Tractor" (2011). Known for blending musical parody, physical comedy, and observational bits on parenting, marriage, and church life, he tours more than 100 shows a year and hosts the podcasts Poddy Break and The Tim Hawkins Podcast with his family. He's self-released an extensive catalog of comedy DVDs, including Full Range of Motion (2007), Insanitized (2010), and Just About Enough (2016), sold primarily through his own site and streaming platform.

Name: Tom Papa
Bio: Stand-up comedian, actor, and podcaster born in Passaic and raised in Woodcliff Lake, New Jersey, now based in Los Angeles. He got his start hosting open mics at New York's Stand Up New York club in the early 1990s, where he met Jerry Seinfeld and was invited to tour with him. Known for warm, everyman observational humor built around his signature line, "Have you ever...? I have!," he's hosted NBC's The Marriage Ref, SiriusXM's Come to Papa, and the podcast Breaking Bread with Tom Papa. He's released a string of specials including Live in New York City (2012), Freaked Out (2013), You're Doing Great! (2020, Netflix), What A Day! (2022, Netflix), and Home Free (2024, Netflix).

Name: Tom Segura
Bio: Stand-up comedian and podcaster born in Cincinnati, Ohio to a Peruvian immigrant mother, raised partly in Minneapolis and Milwaukee before settling in Vero Beach, Florida, now based in Austin, Texas. He got his start as a regional finalist on Last Comic Standing 2 and as an early, frequent guest on The Joe Rogan Experience, before building one of comedy's biggest touring acts with his 300-plus-show "I'm Coming Everywhere" world tour. Known for deadpan, dark observational and insult comedy, he co-hosts the podcast Your Mom's House with his wife, Christina Pazsitzky, and Two Bears, One Cave with Bert Kreischer, and wrote, directed, and starred in the Netflix series Bad Thoughts (2025). He's released six Netflix specials: Completely Normal (2014), Mostly Stories (2016), Disgraceful (2018), Ball Hog (2020), Sledgehammer (2023), and Teacher (2025).

Name: Tommy Little
Bio: Stand-up comedian, radio and TV host from Melbourne, Australia, where he's still based. He studied drama at Deakin University before a friend encouraged him to try stand-up, breaking through on Melbourne's live circuit and debuting at the Melbourne International Comedy Festival in 2009. Known for laid-back, self-deprecating storytelling about his own mishaps, he co-hosted Network 10's The Project for years and has hosted Whose Line Is It Anyway? Australia, A League of Their Own, and Taskmaster Australia. He's released three specials for Amazon Prime Video: Self-Diagnosed Genius (2020), I'll See Myself Out (2021), and Pretty Fly for a Dickhead (2023).

Name: Trevor Noah
Bio: Stand-up comedian, writer, and television host born in Johannesburg, South Africa and raised in Soweto during apartheid, the son of a Xhosa mother and Swiss-German father â€” an origin story he chronicled in his bestselling memoir Born a Crime (2016). He built an early career in South African television and radio before becoming a Daily Show correspondent in 2014 and, months later, Jon Stewart's surprise successor as host, a role he held from 2015 to 2022. Known for globally minded political and cultural satire delivered in multiple languages, he's hosted the Grammy Awards annually since 2021, voiced Griot in Marvel's Black Panther films, and hosts the podcast What Now? with Trevor Noah. His extensive stand-up catalog includes the Netflix specials Afraid of the Dark (2017), Son of Patricia (2018), I Wish You Would (2022), Where Was I (2023), and Joy in the Trenches (2026).

Name: Zoltan Kaszas
Bio: Stand-up comedian born in Budapest, Hungary and raised from age four in Pittsburgh and then San Diego, California, where he still bases his career. He bombed his first open mic in 2006 but stuck with stand-up anyway, later winning the Seattle International Comedy Competition and the San Diego Funniest Person Contest. Known for relatable, observational humor, he became a viral breakout star when a Dry Bar Comedy clip about cats versus dogs drew more than 60 million views on Facebook. He's released a string of specials including Cat Jokes (2017, Dry Bar Comedy), Average Intelligence (2022, Dry Bar Comedy), and the self-released White Lies (2023), Honorary Jones (2024), and London Fog (2025).

Name: Michael Yo
Bio: Stand-up comedian, radio and TV personality born in Houston, Texas to a Black American father and Korean mother, who played football at the University of Arkansas before a concussion history ended that path. He broke into entertainment through Houston radio internships and DJ gigs before becoming an on-air correspondent for E! News, The Daily 10, and Extra, later mentored into stand-up by Chelsea Handler and Jo Koy. Known for clean, corporate-friendly comedy about his multicultural family and upbringing, he's a two-time Emmy nominee, advanced to the quarterfinals of America's Got Talent (Season 15), and holds a weekly residency at Jimmy Kimmel's Comedy Club in Las Vegas. He's released the specials Blasian (2018), I Never Thought (2022), and Snack Daddy (2025).

Name: Shayne Smith
Bio: Stand-up comedian and rock vocalist raised in Fillmore, Utah, who got his start performing at Salt Lake City's Wiseguys Comedy Club in 2014 after cutting his teeth in the local punk music scene as a singer for the band Painted Devils. Named "Best Alternative Comedian of 2016" by Salt Lake City's City Weekly, he's known for goofy, physical, Muppets-influenced comedy built on authentic personal anecdotes rather than cynicism. He co-hosts the podcasts Freaky Geeks and Cowboy Boys, and has released a string of Dry Bar Comedy specials, including Prison for Wizards (2017), Alligator Boys (2019), Banned From Karate (2023), and Ghosts Are Real (2025).

Name: Mario Adrion
Bio: Stand-up comedian born in Alpirsbach, Germany, now based in Los Angeles. A former fashion model who walked runways at New York Fashion Week before pivoting to YouTube comedy in 2017 and stand-up at clubs including the Hollywood Improv and Laugh Factory, he broke through with a viral 2021 American Idol catwalk segment alongside Katy Perry. Known for self-deprecating jokes about being a retired male model navigating America as a European, he's built a following of more than 4 million across social media and hosts the podcast UNCENSORED with Mario Adrion. He released his debut special, My Struggle, in 2026.

Name: Kellen Erskine
Bio: Stand-up comedian known for a calm, deadpan, cerebral style built on mundane topics like banana bread and grocery stores, layered with dense callback jokes. He broke through with a 2018 Just For Laughs Montreal "New Faces" showcase slot and a stand-up debut on Conan, having been named one of TBS's Top Ten Comics to Watch in 2017. A single joke of his about bike locks has drawn tens of millions of views on Dry Bar Comedy clips online. He co-hosts the podcast The Book Pile and has released the specials Composed (2017, Dry Bar Comedy) and Negative Comments (2024, Dry Bar Comedy).

Name: Don McMillan
Bio: Stand-up comedian based in the San Francisco Bay Area, California, and a former electrical engineer with an MS from Stanford who spent 15 years designing microchips at Bell Labs and VLSI Technology before quitting tech to do comedy full-time. He broke through by winning $100,000 as Comedy Grand Champion on Star Search (1993), and returned to the spotlight decades later as a quarterfinalist on America's Got Talent (Season 17, 2022). Billed as "America's #1 Nerdy Comedian," his PowerPoint-driven, tech- and corporate-themed act includes the viral routine "Life After Death by PowerPoint," and he's performed for 800-plus companies including Google, Apple, and Microsoft. He's released the Dry Bar Comedy specials Geek, Nerd or Dork? (2022) and I Am Engineer (2025).

Name: Monique Marvez
Bio: Stand-up comedian born in Miami, Florida to a Cuban/Puerto Rican mother and Venezuelan father, now based in Los Angeles. She began performing in Miami's South Beach clubs at 27, and after being named Miami New Times' "Best New Talent" was invited to the Montreal Comedy Festival, launching her national career; she later spent years as a San Diego radio host. Known as one of the original "Latin Divas of Comedy," she's built her act around frank, sexually candid, culturally rooted material on relationships and family. She's released four Showtime specials and an HBO special, including Not Skinny Not Blonde (2013), based on her book of the same name.

Name: Aaron Woodall
Bio: Stand-up comedian raised in Bowie, Maryland, now based in Salt Lake City, Utah. He started performing stand-up in 2011 while attending Brigham Young University, skipping his own graduation for a bar gig in Wyoming, and broke through in 2018 when he was named to Conan O'Brien's "Comics to Watch" showcase at the New York Comedy Festival. Known for a relatable, vulnerable, yet optimistic style he describes as a "nice young man coming to grips with a dirty, cynical world," he co-hosts the podcast Mormon and the Meth-Head. He's released the specials Unknown (2017, Dry Bar Comedy), Sad and Needy (2020, Comedy Dynamics), and Cry For Me, Daddy (2024, self-released).

Name: Cam Bertrand
Bio: Stand-up comedian born and raised in Tampa, Florida, now based in Austin, Texas, who dropped out of Florida A&M University after three weeks at 19 to pursue comedy full-time, getting his start at open mics in the lobby of Tampa's Side Splitters Comedy Club. In 2019 he became the youngest-ever winner of "Florida's Funniest" and the youngest comedian to record his own Dry Bar Comedy special, later earning unanimous judge approval on America's Got Talent (Season 16, 2021). Known for self-deprecating jokes about his youthful appearance, he's written for MTV's Wild 'N Out and hosts the podcast Hey Let's Complain. His signature special, Sophisticated Ignorance (2019, Dry Bar Comedy), has drawn more than 130 million views.

Name: Brad Upton
Bio: Stand-up comedian born in Richland, Washington, now based in the Seattle area. A former 4th-grade teacher and high school track coach, he first performed stand-up in 1984 and quit teaching two years later to pursue comedy full-time, going on to win the Las Vegas Comedy Festival (2002) and perform at the HBO Comedy Festival at Caesars Palace. Known for clean, broadly relatable "boomer vs. millennial" observational humor, he found viral fame in 2018 when a Dry Bar Comedy clip about millennials became the platform's most-viewed stand-up video ever. A recurring guest at the Grand Ole Opry since 2019, he's released the specials Will Be Funny for Money (2017) and I'm Not Done Yet (2022), both via Dry Bar Comedy.

Name: Matt Falk
Bio: Clean, faith-driven stand-up comedian raised in the Mennonite community of Niverville, Manitoba, now based in Winnipeg, Canada. He started as a teenage magician doing kids' birthday parties before moving into stand-up at 17, becoming the youngest comic ever to headline Winnipeg's Rumor's Comedy Club at 19. Explicitly informed by his Christian faith, his 100%-clean act treats comedy as a form of ministry, and he's been a finalist at the World Series of Comedy and a regular at Just For Laughs Montreal and the Winnipeg Comedy Festival. He's released a string of comedy albums and specials â€” three of which hit #1 on iTunes' Comedy chart â€” including Generational Gap(s) (2018), Un-Lit (2019, Dry Bar Comedy), and Adrenaline and Cortisol (2026).

Name: Chris Martin
Bio: British stand-up comedian and writer raised in Chiswick, West London, now based in Los Angeles. He studied English Literature at Newcastle University, where he began performing at student comedy nights, and broke through with his acclaimed 2011 Edinburgh Fringe solo debut, No. Not That One. Known for whimsical, self-deprecating observational comedy â€” and for good-naturedly clarifying he is not the Coldplay frontman â€” he's written for The Late Late Show with James Corden and Netflix's XO, Kitty, appeared in Netflix's I Think You Should Leave with Tim Robinson, and hosts the podcast Getting My Dad to Say I Love You. He's released the comedy albums All Over the Place (2022) and Above Ground Comedian (2024), the latter also filmed as a full special posted on his YouTube channel.

Name: Myles Weber
Bio: Stand-up comedian born and raised in Vallejo, California, still based in the Vallejo/Fairfield area. He left college at his father's urging to become a physical therapist, instead breaking into comedy at open mics at the now-closed Pepperbellys club in Fairfield, and went on to win the San Francisco International Comedy Competition as one of only two comics ever to sweep the event. Known for high-energy, improv-driven crowd work, he's built a viral following with clips topping 80 million views and was featured on MTV's Greatest Party Story Ever Told. He's released the specials Mr. Bright Side (2021, Comedy Dynamics) and 90's Kind of Love (2025), along with the Dry Bar Comedy specials Pug Life and Dad Lifts.

Name: John Hastings
Bio: Canadian stand-up comedian born in Toronto and raised in Ottawa, who tours internationally across Canada, the US, and the UK. Born three months premature with dyspraxia, a neurological motor-planning disorder he discusses on stage, he went pro in 2010 after years of working telemarketing, coffee shop, and kitchen jobs, and became the youngest comedian ever to perform at the Winnipeg Comedy Festival (2011). He went viral in 2020 with an America's Got Talent audition performed to a nearly empty, COVID-restricted theater, and has since built a reputation as one of comedy's most prolific self-releasers, putting out full specials directly to YouTube at a rapid pace. Known for self-deprecating storytelling about disability and divorce, he co-hosts the podcast John and Dylan Online and has released specials including Everything Goes Wrong (2024, Dry Bar Comedy), The Times They Are a John Hastings (2024), and COMEDIAN JOHN (2025).

Name: Ben Brainard
Bio: Stand-up comedian and social media personality born in 1996 and raised in Ormond Beach, Florida, now based in North Hollywood, California. He dropped out of Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University to join the U.S. Army Reserve, where he began entertaining fellow soldiers with impressions, and started performing stand-up at open mics in Orlando in 2017. He broke through in March 2020 with a viral TikTok video of personified U.S. states discussing COVID-19, launching his long-running sketch series The Table and building a following of millions across TikTok and YouTube. He co-hosts the podcast The Good, The Dan, and the Florida Man and released his debut stand-up special, What a Mature Child (2025), self-released on YouTube.

Name: Andy Woodhull
Bio: Stand-up comedian raised in Northern Indiana who came up through the St. Louis and Chicago comedy scenes. In 2014 he became the first comedian to make his network television debut on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, and has since appeared on Conan and The Late Late Show with James Corden. A stepfather to two daughters, he's built much of his act â€” and several comedy albums â€” around blended-family and stepparenting material. He co-hosts the podcast Backyard Hang and has released the Comedy Central special World's Greatest Stepdad and the Dry Bar Comedy special Middle Parent Syndrome (2024).

Name: Drew Barth
Bio: Stand-up comedian from the Seattle, Washington area, who started doing comedy on a dare in high school before working his way up through Pacific Northwest open mics to clubs, colleges, and casinos, including a stint performing at LA's Comedy Store, Laugh Factory, and The Improv. He was a finalist at the Seattle International Comedy Competition, and in 2018 survived being struck by a car in a crosswalk, undergoing emergency brain surgery and months of recovery that later became stand-up material. Known for relatable, snarky humor about relationships and recovery, he's released the Dry Bar Comedy specials Shoulda Tried Harder (2017) and Tried Too Hard (2023).

Name: Mike Paramore
Bio: Stand-up comedian from Cleveland, Ohio, who played linebacker at Garfield High School and was recruited by the University of Akron before a knee injury ended his football career. While recovering from surgery in Columbus, he stumbled into an improv team and tried a five-minute stand-up set, swearing he'd never do it again before snowballing into a full-time comedy career. Known for energetic, uplifting club comedy, he's won the Cleveland Comedy Festival (2015), the Laughing Devil Festival in New York (2016), and Laugh Fest's Best in the Midwest (2017), and has opened for Damon Wayans and Jon Lovitz. He's released the specials You've Just Been Flirted With (2018, Dry Bar Comedy) and I Probably Shouldn't Say This (2024, Dry Bar Comedy).

Name: Tyler Boeh
Bio: Stand-up comedian from Portland, Oregon, who started as a nationally recognized vocal percussionist and beatboxer in a college a cappella group before transitioning into stand-up on the Portland circuit. He placed in comedy competition finals in Seattle, San Francisco, Boston, and the World Series of Comedy in Las Vegas before relocating to Los Angeles, where he landed two TV pilots within a year. Known for high-energy, physical, silly stand-up that incorporates his award-winning beatboxing, he's appeared on Fox's Laughs and NESN Comedy All-Stars. His debut album, Carpool Companion (2012), was named LaughSpin Magazine's Album of the Year, and he's released the Dry Bar Comedy special Wait for It (2018).

Name: Gabriel Rutledge
Bio: Stand-up comedian born in Bay Center, Washington and raised in South Bend, WA, now based in Olympia, WA. A former decade-long punk rock band member, he left a pizza delivery job in 2000 to pursue comedy full-time, going on to win the Seattle International Comedy Competition (2004) and the Laughing Skull Comedy Festival in Atlanta (2017). Known for observational, family- and marriage-driven humor, he's appeared on Comedy Central's Live at Gotham and Nickelodeon's NickMom Night Out, authored the books Happiness Isn't Funny: True Stories of a Road Comic and There's No F@!*ing Way You're Getting A Pony, and co-hosts the podcast The Rutledges with his wife, Kristi. He's released the specials One Third of the Room (2022, Dry Bar Comedy) and Nectarine (2024).

Name: Rex Havens
Bio: Clean, family-oriented stand-up comedian who holds a JD and MBA and worked as a college business/law professor and corporate attorney before leaving law in 1991 to pursue comedy full-time. Over a three-decade career he's performed in all 50 states and internationally â€” including London, Hong Kong, and Montreal â€” with television credits on Showtime, Comedy Central, and Comic Relief, plus regular appearances on the nationally syndicated Bob & Tom radio show. Known for tasteful, marriage-focused humor, he's released the book and CD Everything I Needed to Know I Learned From My Wife! and a follow-up show, Women & Children First.

Name: Robert G. Lee
Bio: Clean, faith-inflected stand-up comedian raised in Indiana who relocated to Hollywood and spent more than 35 years as one of the industry's most heavily booked network-TV warm-up comedians, working over 1,500 episodes of sitcoms including Cheers, Two and a Half Men, The Drew Carey Show, and Last Man Standing. He got an early break with a role on The Golden Girls, later became a writer for VeggieTales, and wrote and directed the faith-based comedy film Can I Get a Witness Protection? Known for a 100%-clean, family-friendly style he describes as combining a Christian worldview with a Monty Python sensibility, he's released more than ten comedy specials, including Laughter's Still Legal (2020, Dry Bar Comedy), You Need To Apologize For Everything You Didn't Do, and A to Z.

Name: Nick Guerra
Bio: Stand-up comedian from McAllen, Texas, who broke through by winning NBC's 2015 StandUp Showcase and making his TV debut on Comedy Central's Stand Up Revolution with Gabriel Iglesias. He became a fan favorite on NBC's Last Comic Standing and was featured in HBO's Entre Nos series, which led to his own HBO Latino special, Love Me at My Worst (2020), filmed live in San Antonio. Known for personal, relationship-driven storytelling that fans describe as almost cathartic, he's also appeared on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon and released the Dry Bar Comedy special Enjoy Life (2020).

Name: Mike P Burton
Bio: Stand-up comedian raised between North Carolina and Delaware, who earned a theatre degree from Catawba College before moving to New York City, where he paid five dollars for five minutes at his first open mic in the mid-1990s. He built a career as a longtime warm-up comedian for TV talk shows including The Revolution and Bethenny, with fill-in appearances on Rachael Ray, The View, and Dr. Oz. Known for high-energy, personal storytelling â€” including a recurring bit about being "the whitest guy in New York" â€” he's released the Dry Bar Comedy specials I Can Get Whiter (2018) and The Whitest Guy In New York (2020).

Name: Moody Molavi
Bio: Stand-up comedian born in Iran, whose family fled the 1979 Iranian Revolution and settled in Chattanooga, Tennessee in 1981, now based in Tennessee. Billed as a "Southern Baptist Iranian Comedian," he got his start on a dare, winning first place in a local contest against 21 other entrants roughly 14 years ago. His high-energy, family-friendly act mines the collision of his Persian heritage and Southern upbringing, including a bit about his childhood sweetheart-turned-wife becoming his stepsister after their parents married each other. He's released the Dry Bar Comedy specials Remove Before Flight (2019) and Messing With People, along with the comedy album Mood Therapy (2024).

Name: Leland Klassen
Bio: Canadian stand-up comedian with a Mennonite farm-boy background, now based in Abbotsford, British Columbia. Over a three-decade touring career he's hosted the nationally syndicated Popcorn TV and created and hosted Leland Klassen's Comedy Tournament, and recently took a dramatic lead role in the 2025 film Extraordinary. Known for clean, quirky, storytelling-driven comedy, he's appeared on Just for Laughs, the Halifax Comedy Festival, and Netflix's Thou Shalt Laugh. He's released a string of specials including Border Patrol Agents Are Insane (2019, Dry Bar Comedy) and Chapstick Is Lethal (2020, Dry Bar Comedy).

Name: Karen Morgan
Bio: Stand-up comedian born and raised in Athens, Georgia, now based in Cumberland, Maine. A former trial attorney with a law degree from Georgia State, she broke into comedy in 2005 as one of seven finalists out of more than 1,000 entries in Nickelodeon's Search for the Funniest Mom in America. Known for clean, family- and corporate-friendly comedy that draws on her legal career and family life, she's appeared on CBS's The Talk and Gotham Comedy Live and been featured in the Washington Post and HuffPost. She's released the Dry Bar Comedy specials Go Dawgs! (2020), Rub Some Dirt On It (2023), and It's a Miracle Gen X Children Survived (2025).

Name: JJ Barrows
Bio: Stand-up comedian, author, and visual artist born and raised in Pawleys Island, South Carolina. She stumbled into comedy while looking for affordable therapy and instead signed up for a stand-up class, which led a classmate to book her an opening set at Hollywood's The Comedy Store. Known for personal, relatable storytelling about life's ups and downs, she competed at the 2019 Seattle International Comedy Competition and has authored the books it's called a spade and Kinda Funny: Stories by a Full-Time Comedian (with Four Part-Time Jobs). She's released the specials Doodle All Day (2020, Dry Bar Comedy) and The DIY Comedy Special (2021), a self-shot special filmed at home during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Name: Jamie Lissow
Bio: Stand-up comedian from the Rochester, New York area who launched his career in Buffalo clubs after briefly attending University at Buffalo Law School before dropping out, with his father's support, to pursue comedy full-time. His breakthrough came co-starring, co-writing, and co-producing Netflix's Real Rob alongside Rob Schneider, with Adam Sandler, Norm Macdonald, and David Spade appearing across its two seasons. Known for storytelling-driven stand-up praised by Greg Gutfeld as one of the best comedians working today, he's a regular guest on Fox's Gutfeld! and taped a half-hour Comedy Central Presents special in 2009. He's also released the Dry Bar Comedy special Most Absurd Parenting Method, which has drawn more than 20 million views.

Name: Kabir Singh
Bio: Stand-up comedian known as "Kabeezy," born in the Portland, Oregon area to Indian parents, who moved to Mumbai at age 9 before returning to the U.S. at 13 â€” a bicultural whiplash that became the backbone of his act about growing up Indian-American. He made his national stand-up debut on Starz in 2013 and won the 2014 San Francisco International Comedy Competition by taking first place in all five final-round shows, a first in the contest's history, later touring with Jo Koy and Anjelah Johnson and opening for Dave Chappelle and Bill Burr. He reached the Top 15 on America's Got Talent (Season 16, 2021) and wrote for Fox's Family Guy, and released the Dry Bar Comedy specials Stay Single As Long As You Can and Growing Up Indian in America. He died in December 2024 at age 39.

Name: Fred Klett
Bio: Clean, family-friendly stand-up comedian raised in Beloit, Wisconsin, one of ten children in a large Christian family, now based in Wisconsin. A former insurance salesman, he broke into comedy by winning Showtime's "Funniest Man in Milwaukee" contest, launching him into a national touring career and regular spots on Milwaukee's Dave & Carol radio show. Billed as "mom-approved entertainment," he's opened for Jay Leno, Jerry Seinfeld, and Craig Ferguson, and his viral "Women Know Things" bit has drawn more than 40 million views. He's released the specials Fred Klett LIVE!, One of Ten (2018, Dry Bar Comedy), and A Family Affair (2025, Angel Studios).

Name: Dave Nihill
Bio: Stand-up comedian, author, and speaker born and raised in Dublin, Ireland, long associated with the San Francisco comedy scene. He overcame a fear of public speaking by inventing a fictional stage persona, "Irish Dave, an accomplished comedian," spending a year crashing open mics and clubs to learn stand-up techniques he later repurposed for business audiences, and went on to win the San Francisco International Comedy Competition. He's the bestselling author of Do You Talk Funny? 7 Comedy Habits to Become a Better (and Funnier) Public Speaker (2016) and founded the FunnyBizz Conference on storytelling and humor for business. He's released the Dry Bar Comedy special Documented (2019), and has since toured Cultural Appreciation (2023) and Shelf Help (2025).

Name: Dwayne Perkins
Bio: Stand-up comedian born in Brooklyn, New York, now based in Los Angeles, who got his start emceeing in college and performing at Harlem's Uptown Comedy Club before relocating to Boston, where he was scouted and made his TV debut on Late Night with Conan O'Brien in 1999. Known for clean, matter-of-fact observational comedy, he was named one of Rolling Stone's "Five Comics to Watch" in 2012 and served as a regular correspondent on The Jay Leno Show. He's released the Netflix debut special Take Note (2016) and the Dry Bar Comedy special Please Believe It (2017).

Name: Cleto Rodriguez
Bio: Stand-up comedian born and raised in San Antonio, Texas, where he still bases his career, and grandson of Cleto Rodriguez, one of the first Hispanic recipients of the Congressional Medal of Honor. He began performing comedy in 1995 while also working as a morning TV personality on San Antonio's News 4 WOAI, and has since opened for George Lopez, Gabriel Iglesias, and Daniel Tosh. Known for high-energy, clean, observational comedy with a Latino twist on marriage, parenting, and everyday life, he's also active in charitable work supporting wounded veterans and disadvantaged youth. He's released a string of specials including My Name Is Cleto (2019, Dry Bar Comedy) and Cleto Is My Real Name (2021, Comedy Dynamics).

Name: Armando Anto
Bio: Stand-up comedian born and raised in France, now based in Los Angeles, who trained as a classical violinist from age 5 at the French National Conservatory and spent over a decade touring the world as a concert violinist before transitioning into comedy. Billing himself as "the only violinist standup comedian in the world," he blends stand-up with live violin, guitar, and breakdancing, and has competed on NBC's Bring the Funny (2019) and appeared at Just For Laughs (2020). He's released the Dry Bar Comedy specials The Maestro of Comedy (2021) and Politically Confused (2024).

Name: Heath Harmison
Bio: Stand-up comedian from Twin Falls, Idaho, now based in Las Vegas, Nevada, who started comedy about a decade ago at a campus open mic while studying nursing at the College of Southern Idaho. Known for high-energy, family-friendly comedy, he performs regularly on the Las Vegas Strip at venues including Planet Hollywood and the MGM Grand, and his Dry Bar Comedy specials have drawn more than 60 million combined views. He's authored the humor books Father's Easy Answers to Life's Difficult Questions and Mother's Easy Answers to Life's Difficult Questions, and released the specials Raising Insanity (2017), Las Vegas Will Really Mess You Up (2020), and The Pandemic Special (2021).

Name: Steve Soelberg
Bio: Stand-up comedian who grew up in Seattle, Washington and now bases his career in the Salt Lake City, Utah area. He holds a degree in molecular biology and describes himself as "a scientist and a stand-up comedian," building a following through Dry Bar Comedy's touring circuit across 70-plus cities before doing USO tours overseas, and won a Funny or Die competition that landed him a spot on the Oddball Comedy Festival. Known for story-based, observational comedy about everyday inconveniences and awkward personal moments, he released the Dry Bar Comedy special We Say Bim (2017).

Name: Dennis Gaxiola
Bio: Clean stand-up comedian, writer, and evangelist raised in Berkeley, California, the son of a preacher and an Air Force veteran, who tailors material for corporate, church, and club audiences alike. Billed as one of America's funniest clean comedians, he's racked up more than 20 national television appearances, including Comedy Central's Laffapalooza, Gabriel Iglesias Presents Stand-Up Revolution, and BET's ComicView. He's released the Dry Bar Comedy specials Before the Wall Goes Up (2017) and Bible School Dropout (2024).

Name: Bob Smiley
Bio: Clean, family-friendly stand-up comedian based in Houston, Texas, known for a rapid-fire delivery, distinctive high-pitched voice, and self-effacing storytelling about childhood, marriage, and fatherhood. He got his start winning a $500 college stand-up competition before touring as a merchandise manager and MC for Christian rock bands including Newsboys and Third Day, going on to build a two-decade-plus career on the Christian comedy circuit alongside acts like Tim Hawkins and John Crist. Beyond stand-up, he created The Adventures of Average Boy, a recurring feature in Focus on the Family's Clubhouse magazine that's spawned a book series and podcast, and voiced Lowell the Snowman in the 2024 animated film Steal the Naughty List. He's released six comedy specials, including Breaking Bob (2017) and the Dry Bar Comedy specials Tartar Terrorist (2019), Longest Running Dad Joke (2020), and Don't Worry, You're Just Hungry (2021).
